Privacy at Olanga

How the website and Windows app handle your data. The full app privacy notice covers its features, storage and retention in detail.

This website

The product tour records Olanga’s actual interface with sample data and simulated services; timing is edited. It shows a local 1.6.5 preview build, including live-score and Home companion features now available in 1.6.7. Its microphone and text-to-speech were muted, and no real provider request or native desktop edit ran during capture.

Playing the film does not activate your microphone, open your apps, change system volume or contact an AI provider. The film and images are served with the site; there is no third-party video embed. This website does not add advertising trackers, analytics scripts or marketing cookies.

The website’s hosting provider receives ordinary request information, including your IP address, as part of serving the page. Fonts and visual assets are served with the site. Download and source links go to GitHub, which has its own privacy statement.

Voice and cloud features

In the Windows app, wake-word detection runs on your PC. Idle microphone audio is not streamed to an AI provider. With cloud recognition enabled, audio captured for an activated request goes to Google Gemini. Optional Live mode sends microphone audio continuously during that active session. You can mute the microphone or quit the app from its tray menu.

On-device English recognition keeps transcription local and lets you review the transcript. Supported local commands can run without an answer-provider request. Questions and other cloud features may still send the reviewed text and relevant context to Gemini. Shared screenshots, notes and selected project excerpts go to your configured provider when you use the corresponding feature.

If you select NVIDIA Magpie, response text and voice settings go to NVIDIA for speech generation, including spoken responses to local commands.

Desktop tasks send a screenshot of your primary display to Gemini after you approve capture. Choosing an editing region limits where Olanga can act; it does not crop the screenshot that is shared. Review what is visible before capturing and review the proposed steps before allowing edits.

Memory you control

Saved memories live on your computer. Conversational learning uses local rules for a limited set of supported everyday details; it does not train a model. Learning is enabled by default, and you can pause it, inspect what was saved, undo a recent change or delete memories. Relevant enabled memories may accompany cloud requests.

Saved API keys use Windows-backed encryption. Notes, memories and most other personal content are stored locally but are not encrypted by Olanga. The app does not automatically upload analytics or crash reports.

Live scores, Spotify and timers

When you enable live scores, Olanga requests NBA scores and schedules from ESPN. ESPN receives ordinary connection information such as your IP address. Score and schedule caches stay in memory. Unpinning the score card stops its requests.

The Home music card reads Spotify’s Windows media session locally. It pauses polling when you switch tabs or hide Olanga. Timer cards read the deadlines stored on your PC.

Downloads and updates

Checking for updates and downloading installers contacts GitHub. Installation is a separate, user-initiated action. The current Windows installer is unsigned. Its published checksum verifies the file’s bytes, not the publisher’s identity.

Questions

You can raise a privacy or product question in the project issue tracker. Issues are public: keep API keys, private recordings, screenshots and profile files out of them.
